title: OrgSwift normalized org-mode JSON tree
description: Formal JSON Schema for the expected.json shape documented in SCHEMA.md. Every conformance/*/expected.json file, and any parser's parseOrg() output meant to conform, is a single value matching $defs/node (the document root is itself a node of type "document"). See schema/README.md for how to run this schema against a file, and ADAPTER.md at the repo root for the full contract a new parser implementation needs.

postBlank.description: org-element's :post-blank, kept as an explicit field per SCHEMA.md section 1. Present on every node except the bare text leaf.

tblfm.description: org-element's :tblfm on a table -- the `#+TBLFM:' formula line or lines, which org-element folds INTO the table element rather than leaving as a sibling keyword node (no keyword node is produced for a TBLFM line at all). null when absent, otherwise one string per line. THE ARRAY IS IN REVERSE SOURCE ORDER: source order `AAA' then `BBB' comes back ["BBB", "AAA"], because org-element's table parser builds the list with `push' during a forward scan and its own interpreter re-emits it through an explicit (reverse ...). It is kept reversed here rather than tidied, per SCHEMA.md section 1's rule to carry org-element's own tree -- so a RENDERER must emit the lines in reverse of this array, exactly as Emacs does. Trailing spaces after a formula are captured inside the string. Carried by table.el tables as well as org tables, which is why both table shapes require it.

affiliated.description: SCHEMA.md section 5. An ORDERED array of {key, value} entries, one per distinct affiliated key, in source first-occurrence order -- the order is schema data (org-element retains it as plist key order; measured on Emacs 30.2, forward and reversed probes). A repeated key GROUPS at its first occurrence position with its values in source order; org-element itself cannot represent interleaved repeats (SCHEMA.md section 10's interleaved-grouping loss). Per-key value shapes: NAME and PLOT are plain strings (last occurrence wins). HEADER is an array of strings, one per #+HEADER: line in source order (a multiple keyword, not dual). CAPTION is an array of {long, short} entries, one per #+CAPTION: line in source order (both a multiple AND a dual keyword) -- long is always an array of object-nodes, short is a string or null depending on whether the #+CAPTION[short]: long dual form was used. RESULTS is always {value, hash} -- hash is a string only when the #+RESULTS[hash]: name dual form was used, null otherwise. ATTR_<BACKEND> (any backend name, e.g. ATTR_HTML, ATTR_LATEX) is an array of strings, one per repeated #+ATTR_<BACKEND>: line, matched by a key pattern since the backend name is open-ended. The oneOf ties each key to its value shape; an unrecognized key here is a bug in the generator, not a schema gap.

date.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Timestamps. A plain nested value, not a schema node in its own right: no "type" key, no postBlank.

rep.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Timestamps. Repeater or delay. Also a plain nested value: its own "type" key is data (the repeater/delay kind), not a schema-node discriminant, and it has no postBlank.

node.description: Any schema node, element or object. SCHEMA.md section 6: the object-vs-element restriction on WHERE a given type may appear is a parser concern, not a JSON-shape concern (a table-cell's children and a paragraph's children have the identical JSON shape), so this union is deliberately flat rather than split into separate ElementNode/ObjectNode unions. Implemented as an if/then/else dispatch on "type" (NOT oneOf across all alternatives) -- see schema/README.md "Why if/then, not oneOf" for the performance reason: a flat oneOf across ~38 shared-shape alternatives is combinatorially expensive to validate (every non-matching branch still recursively re-validates shared keys like "children"), which is empirically confirmed to blow up to 30+ seconds on a single small nested fixture and would only get worse on deeper real-world trees. if/then dispatches on the type tag directly: exactly one branch's full schema is ever evaluated per node.

document.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. The tree root. children: [section?, headline*].

headline.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. children: [section?, headline*], one level down.

trueLevel.description: org-element's :true-level -- the RAW leading-star count. Differs from `level' above only under `#+STARTUP: odd' (org-odd-levels-only), where org-element REDUCES :level: `*** B' reports level 2, trueLevel 3. Two different star counts can collapse onto one `level' (`** B' and `*** B' both report level 2), so `level' alone cannot reconstruct the source. Always present, always an integer.

section.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. Omitted entirely by the parser when it would be empty (see section 3) -- this schema describes the node's own shape when present, it cannot enforce the omission rule itself.

planning.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. scheduled/deadline/closed are always present keys, each a timestamp node or null.

clock.description: SCHEMA.md section 4. CLOCK: line. value is the timestamp node or null (a duration-only CLOCK: => 12:34 line has none); duration is the H:MM string or null. status is derivable (closed exactly when duration is non-null) and deliberately not stored.

node-property.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. key is the :NAME: without colons; value can be an empty property's null.

drawer.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. A generic :NAME:...:END: drawer other than PROPERTIES, e.g. LOGBOOK.

dynamic-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 9 (latex-fragment and dynamic-block). #+BEGIN: NAME ARGS...#+END:. arguments is the raw, unparsed rest-of-line text, or null.

special-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4. #+begin_TYPE PARAMS block whose TYPE org does not recognize. blockType keeps the SOURCE case of the name; parameters is the trimmed rest of the opener line, null when empty. Contents are elements, same as quote/center blocks.

quote-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. A greater element: children are element nodes (paragraph, list, ...), not raw objects.

center-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. Same shape as quote-block.

verse-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Structural. Unique among blocks: children are object nodes directly (text markup, links, timestamps, ...), not elements. A verse line boundary is a literal "\n" inside a text node's own value, not a separate node type.

paragraph.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Text-level container objects. children: object nodes.

text.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Text-level container objects. Leaf. The ONLY node type with no postBlank key at all: org-element tracks post-blank only on proper element/object nodes, and a bare plain-text span is not one.

bold.description: SCHEMA.md section 4/6/7. children: object nodes; may nest italic/underline/strikethrough/links/code/verbatim/entities/sub-superscript.

italic.description: Same shape as bold, see SCHEMA.md sections 4/6/7.

underline.description: Same shape as bold, see SCHEMA.md sections 4/6/7. Documented but not given its own Layer 1 fixture (SCHEMA.md section 7 rule 1).

strikethrough.description: Same shape as bold, see SCHEMA.md sections 4/6/7. Documented but not given its own Layer 1 fixture (SCHEMA.md section 7 rule 1).

code.description: SCHEMA.md section 4. Leaf, always literal: never further parsed for emphasis or links.

verbatim.description: Same shape as code, see SCHEMA.md section 4.

entity.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Misc. \alpha / \alpha{}. `name` + `useBrackets` fully determine the source bytes (org-element-entity-interpreter emits backslash, name, and {} when bracketed). The six per-entity renderings (:latex, :html, :ascii, ...) are the org-entities table row for `name` and are deliberately NOT duplicated here.

name.description: org-element's :name -- the exact table key, e.g. "alpha", "frac12", "_ " (the whitespace entities' names contain literal spaces).

useBrackets.description: org-element's :use-brackets-p -- true when the source wrote \name{} and the braces were consumed.

target.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Misc. <<anchor>>. Leaf: `value` is the text between the angle pairs; org-element-target-interpreter re-emits exactly <<value>>.

macro.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Misc. {{{name(args)}}}. Leaf: `value` is the ENTIRE source text, case intact. org-element's :key (downcased) and :args are deterministic functions of `value` and are not duplicated. org's own interpreter rebuilds from :key and loses the name's case; renderOrg emits `value` verbatim.

link.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Links. description is null (not []) when the link has no description -- the one field in this schema where null and empty-array are meaningfully different.

pathType.description: org-element's own :type -- how the PATH is to be read: "https", "mailto", "file", "id", "custom-id", "fuzzy", "coderef", "radio", or any other registered link type. Orthogonal to `linkType' above (which carries org-element's :format): a radio link is pathType "radio" with linkType "plain", and capturing it is the only thing that keeps a radio link distinguishable from an ordinary plain link. Always a non-empty string. NAMING WART, stated rather than hidden: org's own manual calls :type the link type, so the reference-faithful names would be `linkType' for :type and `format' for :format -- this schema's `linkType' is named after the wrong property. Renaming it was rejected deliberately, because silently changing the meaning of a published field name is worse for consumers than an imperfect new name.

item.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Lists. bullet is the literal bullet text used ("-", "+", "1.", "a)"). tag is only meaningful for descriptive lists. children is the item's body (element nodes).

counter.description: org-element's :counter -- the explicit `[@N]' counter override, e.g. the 5 in `1. [@5] five'. An INTEGER, not the raw source text, and null when the item has no override. Set on unordered items too (`- [@5]'). Lossy for the alphabetical form: `1. [@c]' and `1. [@C]' both give 3, since org-element converts a letter to its alphabet index -- a declined loss recorded in SCHEMA.md section 10.

src-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Blocks. value is org-element's own :value, unmodified -- literal text between the #+begin_src/#+end_src lines, including the trailing newline after the last content line.

switches.description: org-element's :switches -- the flag string between the language and the header arguments, e.g. "-n -r" in `#+begin_src elisp -n -r'. Independent of `params': `#+begin_src elisp -n -r :tangle yes' gives switches "-n -r" and params ":tangle yes". null when absent.

example-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Blocks. Same value convention as src-block.

switches.description: org-element's :switches, same shape and convention as src-block's, e.g. "-n" in `#+begin_example -n'. null when absent. src-block and example-block are the ONLY two block types org-element tracks :switches on.

export-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Blocks. backend is the #+begin_export line's backend token (e.g. "HTML"), or null.

comment-block.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Blocks. Same value convention as src-block.

comment.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Blocks. A single "# ..." line. The marker "#" and exactly one following space are stripped from value.

keyword.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Keywords. A standalone #+KEY: VALUE line whose key is not one of the recognized affiliated-keyword names (or is, but was not immediately followed by an eligible element). key is always uppercase.

horizontal-rule.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Misc. Leaf, no value, no children: a line of 5+ consecutive "-".

statistics-cookie.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Misc. Leaf, e.g. "[1/3]" or "[50%]".

useBrackets.description: org-element's :use-brackets-p -- which SOURCE form was written: false for `a_b', true for `a_{b}'. Without it the two forms normalize to an identical tree. Always present. Named without the Lisp predicate `-p', following `commented' from `:commentedp' on headline.
org-element's :use-brackets-p -- which SOURCE form was written: false for `a^b', true for `a^{b}'. Same convention as subscript's.

table.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Tables, plus C3 (table.el). Two mutually exclusive shapes, mirroring exactly what harness/oracle-dump.el's `table' branch emits: an ordinary org-mode pipe table carries `children' ([table-row*], every table in this corpus uses this form), a table.el (ASCII-bordered) table carries `value' (the raw literal text) instead - org-element never decomposes a table.el table into rows/cells, so there is nothing to put in `children' for it. The two branches are distinguished by which of `children'/`value' is present, not by a `kind'/`tableType' discriminator field - that was tried and deliberately reverted (see schema/README.md, "Why clock and table.el stay unmapped"). Before this fix, this definition only accepted the children-shape, so a table.el node correctly emitted by the generator was incorrectly rejected by the schema meant to describe it - the same class of bug the keyword/affiliated fix corrected.

table-row.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Tables. kind "rule" is a |---+---| separator row and always has an empty children array.

table-cell.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Tables. children: object nodes. The single formatting space around | padding is a corpus-authoring convention, not part of any node's text.

timestamp.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Timestamps. end is non-null only for the two -range kinds. start is null only for the diary kind (SCHEMA.md section 9), which has no year/month/day to report. diarySexp is present (a string, the raw "(SEXP ...)" text, e.g. "(diary-float 1 3 2)") only when kind is "diary" -- absent entirely, not null, for every other kind, matching org-element's own behavior (it does not track :diary-sexp on non-diary timestamps at all, the same kind of absence :pre-blank has on paragraph/plain-list).

rangeType.description: org-element's :range-type -- which SOURCE form produced a range. "timerange" is a single timestamp with an internal time-time contraction (`<2026-01-01 Thu 10:00-12:00>'); "daterange" is a genuine two-full-timestamp range (`<date>--<date>'). null for the non-range kinds and for diary. This is also what explains a null `end.dayname' on a timerange: a timerange's raw value carries exactly one dayname token, so null is reference-faithful rather than a gap (SCHEMA.md section 10, item 12).

footnote-reference.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Footnotes (documented, not yet in the Layer 1 corpus). label is null only for an anonymous inline footnote. children is present ONLY when inline is true -- absent entirely, not an empty array, when inline is false.

footnote-definition.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Footnotes (documented, not yet in the Layer 1 corpus). children: element nodes.

latex-fragment.description: SCHEMA.md section 9 (latex-fragment and dynamic-block). Leaf, same shape as code/verbatim: value is the fragment's own literal text, delimiters included (e.g. "$x^2$").

latex-environment.description: SCHEMA.md section 4. \begin{NAME}...\end{NAME} LaTeX environment. A leaf: value is the raw byte run from the opener line through the closer line, indentation and trailing whitespace intact, re-emitted verbatim.

line-break.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Misc. A forced line break -- a line ending in `\\'. Carries NEITHER `value' NOR `children': like horizontal-rule, its entire meaning is its type (SCHEMA.md section 1's third node shape). org-element's own line-break parser builds the node with only :begin, :end and :post-blank, so there is no other property to read. RENDERER NOTE: the newline belongs to THIS node, not to the following text -- org-element's own line-break interpreter returns the literal string backslash-backslash-newline, so a renderer emits all three characters from this node alone and must not also emit a newline for the line ending here, or it double-counts.

radio-target.description: SCHEMA.md section 4, Links. `<<<target>>>' -- the anchor a radio link matches against. A container carrying `children' only, never `value', even though org-element gives a radio-target BOTH a :value holding the raw text and parsed object contents at the same time: section 1 forbids one node having both, and `children' is the lossless choice (the children re-emit to exactly the :value text, and nested markup inside the target survives, which :value would flatten).
